A useful little stand.
For our technology afternoon, each group prepared something useful. Our group chose to make stands that could hold a tablet during a presentation. The stands were made from used boxes, so we did not need new plastic. Our teacher cut the shapes, and we added colors and labels. At first, my stand was too low. When I put the tablet on it, the screen was difficult to see. Jo suggested a different shape. We tried it with an empty case first, then our teacher checked the finished stand. The second design worked much better. Sam took photographs of the steps. A guide was printed in the computer room, with one photograph beside each short instruction. We wanted other pupils to follow the process easily. On the afternoon of the display, a younger group came to our table. One pupil asked who made the stand. I explained that the shape was cut by our teacher and the design was tested by our group. Nobody made the whole thing alone. The visitors liked the guide because its pictures were clear. I learned that technology does not always mean an expensive machine. A simple object can solve a problem when its design is carefully tested.
